note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; referenced benefits include source quotations and contextual paraphrases, not estimates for this plant.

questions.question: What do existing records establish about these cooling/steam-labelled candidates' process-stream duties and any system-level heat-integration question?

data_requests.item: Existing exact process-stream identities, temperature-enthalpy and duty basis
where: only a valve (HV-112) is drawn on this line, with no flow measurement; flow needs a meter or a calibrated valve curve
historian or DCS trend for FT-106 (no historian tag is mapped in this model for these)

site records: Existing process/utility identities and directions, actual supply/target temperatures, flows, heat-capacity/phase/duty and operating coverage for each represented cooling and steam candidate; source/revision/availability, quantity units and matching sample periods retained.

a walkdown: Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no compulsory new measurement, production stop, setpoint change or retrofit.
data_requests.how: A CW or steam valve/instrument label is a proxy, not measured process heat rejection/heating, a process-stream identity or a flow signal. Retain each owner/source separately, including related steam-record values shown as candidate evidence. Review actual comparable process duties and uncertainty before inferring any match; command values, foreign data or incompatible units/periods cannot settle it.

data_requests.item: Existing process-wide targets and time-aware operating constraints
where: site records: Existing heat/material balance, process-wide temperature-enthalpy/composite profiles and utility targets, batch sequences and timing, current studies and alternatives, with source scope and economic/operating assumptions.

a walkdown: Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no compulsory new measurement, production stop, setpoint change or retrofit.
data_requests.how: S19 printed43-45 describes process-wide composite curves, approach/capital-energy tradeoffs and developments for batch/time-aware integration and heat pumps/transformers. Do not replace that analysis with a rule that all hot temperatures must exceed all cold temperatures, or automatically close every non-simultaneous/batch pair. Conversely, overlapping ideal profiles or an alternative technology name is not proof of feasible recovery. Review the appropriate system and timing model before deciding.

data_requests.item: Existing physical, material, fouling and hazard/feasibility basis
where: site records: Existing layout/routing and fouling/cleaning records, composition/pressure/material and cross-contamination constraints, reactive/process hazard review, existing exchanger/network function and economic/practical basis; authority and missing records remain explicit.

a walkdown: Only if existing records leave an applicable question unresolved, agree safe additional observations with the responsible engineer; no compulsory new measurement, production stop, setpoint change or retrofit.
data_requests.how: Existing suitable studies may be acknowledged without new measurements or a compulsory exchanger study. On reactive service an integration change needs the applicable hazard review; a missing review, supplied Boolean or source label is not protection acceptance. No piping connection, operating change, whole-process completeness or site saving follows from the represented pair.

questions.decision_rule: Review the actual process-wide temperature-enthalpy/utility targets, stream identities and duty/time basis, practical approach/capital tradeoffs and physical/material/hazard constraints before an integration decision. Do not prescribe a connection or automatically close a question from a pairwise temperature-range, simultaneity, hours or distance shortcut. Suitable existing analysis or nonapplicability may be acknowledged; missing or contradictory source/units/time remains explicit.

typical_benefit.wording: The source describes systematic process-wide temperature-enthalpy targeting and matching of heating/cooling demands, including time-aware batch approaches and alternatives. Potential depends on the actual process and capital-energy tradeoffs; this screen establishes no universal superiority, quantified benefit or site saving.

questions.limits: The represented cooling-water and other-unit steam labels are screening proxies, not established process-stream duties or a feasible heat match. Review process-wide temperature-enthalpy targets, duty/time coverage and practical constraints; pairwise temperature ranges or simultaneity alone do not decide broader integration potential. On a reactive system any heat-integration change needs a hazard review first. IAC/ITAC figures are browse-page averages read through a summarizing fetch and not re-verified against the downloadable database; averages are skewed by outliers. Source review: original LBNL-56183 printed43-45/PDF51-53 from the official ENERGY STAR mirror; raw equivalence to inaccessible catalog OSTI bytes is not claimed. The original far-exceeds comparative quotation remains historical; it is not evidence for this pair or a guarantee. Reactive-system hazard-review requirement is retained.
